clips.alt: MagicSchool — MagicSchool: check questions and answers: recorded demonstration and use.
clips.caption: MagicSchool · 50.7 s
clips.prompt: Create five questions on the supplied chapter summary for second-year university students. Test training versus inference, a definition added to a prompt, tokens versus words, RAG versus parameter updates, and next-token probability versus truth. Provide the answer key and a brief rationale. Avoid trick questions. Source summary: training changes parameters; ordinary inference uses fixed parameters; a new prompt changes context; a token may be a word, word part or punctuation; RAG supplies retrieved passages as context and does not guarantee correctness; token probability measures a possible continuation, not the factual truth of the whole answer. Answer in English. Keep questions concise and provide one short rationale per correct answer.

clips.alt: MagicSchool — MagicSchool: draft and review a rubric: recorded demonstration and use.
clips.caption: MagicSchool · 58.6 s
clips.prompt: Create a four-level rubric for a second-year university student who studies the workshop chapter, builds a labelled diagram and independently explains language-model generation. Use exactly three criteria: concepts and relationships; process explanation; application and checking. Describe observable evidence at each level. Distinguish the assisted product from the independent explanation. Do not reward writing polish or code complexity alone. Source distinctions: training updates numerical parameters; ordinary inference uses fixed parameters; adding a prompt definition changes context; RAG supplies retrieved passages as context and does not itself update weights; next-token probability is not a guarantee of truth.

clips.alt: Formative — Formative: build and preview an assessment: recorded demonstration and use.
clips.caption: Formative · 146.7 s
clips.prompt: Create three questions for a private workshop demonstration, in English. Use only these chapter facts: training updates model parameters; ordinary inference keeps parameters fixed; a new prompt changes context; RAG supplies retrieved passages as context. Q1 Multiple Choice: During ordinary inference, what changes when a new prompt is entered? Options: A The original training data; B The available context; C The learned parameters. Correct answer B, 1 point. Q2 Free Response: Andrea says that adding a definition to the prompt updates the model weights. Explain the error in two sentences. Expected: context changes, learned parameters remain fixed during ordinary inference. Q3 Drawing: Draw and label prompt plus context -> inference with fixed parameters -> next token. Add a brief note explaining what changes when a definition is added. Use only these three basic question types. This is an authored example; no real student records.

clips.prompt: Plan a 20-minute university lesson using the workshop chapter on training, inference and RAG. Goal: independently explain what changes in each process. Include a diagnostic question, a short source-reading activity, a labelled diagram, a misconception check and a two-minute exit ticket. Give timings and expected evidence. Source distinctions: training updates numerical parameters; ordinary inference keeps the learned parameters fixed; prompt changes affect context; RAG retrieves passages and adds them to context, without itself retraining the model. Include a simpler prompt for a learner who confuses context with parameters, keeping the same learning goal.
clips.observed: Generated a 20-minute lesson with a 2/4/5/7/2-minute sequence, learner evidence, a simpler prompt and an accurate exit-ticket key; copied the editable document text.
clips.scope: Actual MagicSchool execution on authored workshop distinctions. The plan is a draft for teacher review. The diagnostic wording “inside the model” needs clarification; an individual diagnostic check is retained before source work. No classroom learning effect was measured. Account plan not established.
